The download graph now paints correctly at gigabit speeds.

### Fixed
- **Download graph rendered at a fraction of its height at high speeds.** Root cause is an integer overflow in JDownloader's graph painting (AppWork `Graph`): every sample is plotted as `(int)(height * value * 0.9) / max` with `value` in raw bytes/s — the `height * value` product is a 32-bit multiplication that overflows above ~34 MiB/s (at the 64px row this image uses; ~67 MiB/s at JD's stock 32px). Overflowed samples wrap low or clip away entirely, and the speed-limit line vanishes (only its red text stays). The bundled GUI agent now hides the native speed meter and paints its own graph with 64-bit arithmetic: **full height at any speed**, same look (theme colours, average overlay, speed-limit band, localized texts). The native panel stays alive underneath, so its speed-limit menu keeps working (clicks are forwarded).
- CI hygiene: the icon asset workflow no longer runs (and fails) on tag pushes.

### Update
Pull `ghcr.io/junkerderprovinz/jdownloader:latest` (or `junkerderprovinz/jdownloader:latest` on Docker Hub) and recreate the container — in Unraid: **Force Update**. The log prints `[jd-dialog-agent] replaced the speed graph (native math overflows above ~34 MiB/s)` once active.
